title: Proactive Straggler Detection and Kernel-Model Matching for Continuous Batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce prefill and decode tail latency by combining an online straggler predictor with per-request kernel-model matching and adaptive admission decisions. The goal is to lower p95/p99 latency for mixed workloads while preserving throughput/cost targets. This ticket prototypes a lightweight straggler score, integrates it into admission control, and adds a kernel compatibility lookup that prefers kernels with lower long-tail variance for predicted-straggler batches.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented straggler predictor deployed behind feature flag and returning per-request scores in runtime logs
Admission controller uses predictor to route or split batches and enforces per-batch tail-latency budget
Kernel-model lookup returns prioritized kernel variants for predicted straggler requests and is exercised in CI microbenchmarks
End-to-end perf: 20% reduction in p99 prefill latency for 99th percentile heavy-tail workload without >5% throughput loss
Runbook updated and canary rollout plan documented; feature flag rollback verified
technical_notes: Approach: 1) Train a small logistic regression / light GBM on streaming telemetry (sequence length, tokens_so_far, model_variant, client_tier, queue_delay, recent_kv_cache_hits) to predict probability that a request will be a tail (costly prefill or decode). 2) Expose score as 'straggler_score' in request metadata. 3) Extend admission controller to: a) preemptively place high-score requests in smaller batches or single-slot flow; b) select kernel variants with lower variance (e.g., 8-bit matmul microkernel vs default fused kernel) for batches containing >X% high-score requests; c) optionally execute a fast-path decoding kernel for predicted short decodes. 4) Add safety: cap the fraction of single-slot prefill to preserve throughput; backoff policy if throughput SLO violated. Trade-offs: more single-slot work increases GPU utilization inefficiency and may raise cost. We will tune thresholds from offline sims and live canary metrics.
experiments: exp/2025-02-12/lightgbm-training-v1: 50k traces, features listed in technical_notes, ROC-AUC 0.79 on 24h holdout
bench/2025-02-15/canary-gpu-a: baseline p99 prefill=420ms, with naive splitter p99=360ms (-14%) throughput -1.2%
bench/2025-02-20/kernel-variant-A: prioritized microkernel for stragglers reduced variance by 28% in synthetic long-tail workload
validation/2025-02-22/ci-micro: unit tests for kernel lookup + admission logic added in runtime-acceptance suite
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy predictor as non-enforcing telemetry-only for 48h to validate score distribution; 2) Enable admission adjustments behind feature flag targeting 1% of traffic (canary); 3) Expand to 10% after 24h if p95/p99 improve and throughput within targets; 4) Enable kernel matching in parallel behind separate flag and run A/B comparing cost and latency; 5) Gradual ramp to 100% with weekly guardrail checks and automated rollback on anomalies.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictor false positives can force too many single-slot prefills and hurt throughput. Mitigation: conservative thresholding, hard cap on single-slot fraction, and automatic scaling to absorb load. Risk: Kernel variant may degrade quality for some model variants. Mitigation: restrict matching to model-kernel pairs validated in perf/quality matrix and include a quality sanity-check in canary. Risk: increased scheduler complexity and operational burden. Mitigation: instrumented dashboards and automatic fallback to current admission logic.
